exposure: gestational week at delivery (28-33 weeks vs. 34-36 weeks)
time interval from premature rupture of membranes (PROM) to delivery (<48h vs. >=48h)
outcome: delivery methods (vaginal delivery, assisted vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 400 single pregnant primiparous women with premature rupture of membranes (PROM) at 28-36 weeks of gestation.
finding: In primiparous women with PROM, a greater gestational week at delivery is associated with a lower rate of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, while a longer time interval between membrane rupture and delivery is associated with a higher rate of adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: The proportion of vaginal delivery was significantly higher in women delivering at 28-33 weeks (Group A) compared to those delivering at 34-36 weeks (Group B), which had higher rates of assisted vaginal delivery and cesarean section.
